scope: Common-model event delegates, generated Host selection and typed listeners, fixed $events/$events/result, current reverse agent Context resolution, owned/borrowed settlement and standard .NET/TS consumption.

commits.change: Connect event authoring, generation, runtime and consumers.
Settle queued source invocations on withdrawal; update the package service inventory.
Declare the disposable standard lib and admit the selected event endpoint in the browser fixture.
Make actual Context preparation independent of cached client output.

retained: One common declaration model, current Registry adapters, existing Connection and Cordis events, configuration/management operations and installation task lifetimes. No new dependency, model format generation or compatibility path.
publicUse: Declare a RemoteEvent delegate, select its generated Definition or Forward projection once on the Host, and use generated typed On listeners. Business InvokeAsync passes its subject; callers do not supply agentId. RemoteEventResult<T> distinguishes continuation from business undefined and null.

failedEvidence.observation: Queued waterfall withdrawal left two of three calls pending; the added regression timed out before repair.
An overlapping diagnostic test locked Windows output DLLs during the first build attempt. Subsequent runs used independent outputs or waited for the owner to exit.
Package inspection retained the old three-service count after the notification Remote was removed.
The strict independent CLR multi-entry TS consumer rejected Symbol.dispose without a declaration-owned standard-lib reference.
A clean Linux consumer could not import a cached client bundle. The driver now bundles the actual vendored Context in its isolated output.

browser.boundary: Real recovery/withdrawal UI only. The final change is solely the independent verification driver; the browser result is not relabelled as a new execution.

format.checkpoint: withdrawal repair before the browser fixture admission edit

remaining: Direct Gateway operatorPeer fallback, browser scoped consumption, remaining model backends and named platform integrations remain open.
